We’re building a world of health around every individual — shaping a more connected, convenient and compassionate health experience. At CVS Health®, you’ll be surrounded by passionate colleagues who care deeply, innovate with purpose, hold ourselves accountable and prioritize safety and quality in everything we do. Join us and be part of something bigger – helping to simplify health care one person, one family and one community at a time.
Job Description
The Sr Data Scientist, Clinical Intelligence supports Medical Affairs by translating Caremark and Retail Pharmacy claims, dispensing, adjudication, and related data into clinically meaningful measures and actionable analyses. The role helps evaluate medication access, affordability, adherence, persistence, utilization, formulary performance, safety, and outcomes.
This individual contributor will contribute to recurring dashboards and key performance indicators as well as focused therapy-class, program, and product analyses. The role works under the direction of the VP, Data Strategy & Clinical Intelligence and partners with Caremark, Retail, Clinical Evidence Development, product, clinical, finance, technology, and analytics stakeholders.
Primary Job Duties & Responsibilities
· Applies SQL, statistical programming, and visualization tools to explore, analyze, and interpret large pharmacy datasets and solve defined clinical and business problems.
· Develops and maintains analytical frameworks, key metrics, and dashboard content related to medication access, affordability, adherence, utilization, formulary performance, quality, clinical outcomes, and operational performance.
· Translates stakeholder questions into documented analytic specifications, including eligible populations, treatment definitions, drug-code lists, index dates, baseline and follow-up periods, outcomes, and exclusions.
· Works with PBM and related client, member, drug, pharmacy, prescriber, prior-authorization, and payment data.
· Uses NDC, GPI, generic product, brand, therapeutic class, route, and other drug reference information to create and validate medication cohorts.
· Analyzes formulary compliance, preferred product use, generic and biosimilar adoption, exceptions, prior authorization, approval and overturn patterns, member out-of-pocket cost, specialty utilization, and other access or affordability measures.
· Partners with Clinical Evidence Development on feasibility assessments, exposure definitions, comparator selection, adherence measures, outcomes, confounding assessment, validation, and interpretation.
· Collaborates with the Sr. BI Engineer to operationalize validated measures and analytic datasets in governed, automated reporting products.
· Follows privacy, client-data segregation, security, access, and data governance requirements for protected health information and confidential business data.
Minimum Requirements
· 2 to 4 years of relevant experience in pharmacy analytics, PBM analytics, healthcare data science, pharmacoepidemiology, outcomes research, clinical informatics, or a related field.
· Experience working with pharmacy claims, dispensing data, medication utilization, or adherence measures.
· Proficiency in SQL and working proficiency in R, Python, SAS, or another statistical programming language.
· Working knowledge of drug identifiers and classifications such as NDC, GPI, generic product, brand, and therapeutic class.
· Experience developing dashboards, KPI frameworks, analytic datasets, or decision-support analyses.
· Working knowledge of problem solving and decision making, with strong attention to data detail and analytic accuracy.
· Ability to communicate technical and clinical findings to nontechnical stakeholders.
Preferred Qualifications
· Experience PBM data
· Knowledge of claims adjudication, prior authorization, formulary operations, specialty pharmacy, retail pharmacy, rebates, or net-cost concepts.
· Experience implementing PDC, persistence, PQA, CMS Star medication, formulary, biosimilar, or member-affordability measures.
· Experience with Google Cloud Platform, Tableau, Power BI, or Strategy.
Education
Bachelor's degree or equivalent specialized training or relevant professional qualification preferred. Advanced training in biostatistics, epidemiology, pharmacoepidemiology, health services research, public health, pharmacy, data science, informatics, statistics, or a related field is desirable.

At Forterra, we are unleashing autonomy at scale to transform the battlefield. About the role
Forterra is building RF statistical-learning techniques for difficult, real-world sensing environments. The work combines signal processing, statistical learning, and carefully designed experiments to recognize and understand signals in conditions where clean textbook data is not enough.

We are hiring a technical research lead who wants to make a visible impact. You will take ambitious ideas from mathematical formulation through working techniques, testing, and operationally relevant evaluation. You will work closely with RF and DSP engineers, platform engineers, and analysts who use the results. This is a hands-on, mid-career applied-research role for someone who enjoys moving between signal processing, statistical learning, numerical methods, and experimental design. You should be excited by hard, imperfect data; eager to learn from failures; and motivated to see your work shape real systems.

• Build a disciplined data practice: versioned datasets and splits, label quality rules, leakage checks, and reproducible training and evaluation recipes. Make synthetic, simulated, and collected data distinguishable in every result.

• Design synthetic and hybrid data generation that exercises the technique's intended operating envelope, then characterize where synthetic performance does and does not transfer to collected data.

• Run training and ablation studies; diagnose failures as data, labeling, representation, optimization, technique, or evaluation problems; and make the next experiment smaller and more informative.

• Establish meaningful technique qualification: held-out and stress evaluation, calibration, confusion analysis, uncertainty behavior, tail failures, and clear criteria for whether a technique is ready to move forward.

• Own the mapping from learned signal behavior to consistent, structured event and object descriptions, with explicit evidence rules, so that technique outputs can be understood and acted upon.
